In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether a standard lymph drainage field (RTOG) is sufficient for salvage radiotherapy after radical prostatectomey and lymphadenectomy.
the evaluation of the impact of 68Ga-PSMA PET imaging on radiotherapy planning for patients with recurrent prostate cancer after radical prostatectomies and lymph node dissections.
the question of whether a 68Ga PSMa PET imaging based radiation planning concept would be able to improve outcome compared to the standard radiation therapy planning after RPE and LAD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of 68Ga PET/CT imaging in recurrent prostate cancer has the potential to change the treatment paradigm and to increase the efficacy of salvage radiotherapy.
68Ga PSMa PET imaging has the potential to improve the outcome of SRT after RPE and LNA.
68Ga PSMa PET is a highly accurate imaging modality for detection of recurrent prostate cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of 68Ga-PSMA PET/CT for radiation therapy planning of patients with recurrent prostate cancer is a promising tool to improve treatment outcome.
68Ga PSma PET imaging is a useful tool for radiation planning in prostate cancer patients after RPE and that it should be considered in the treatment planning of recurrent prostate cancer patients.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a standard RT field after RPE and lymphadenectomy does not cover all sites of recurrence.
68Ga PSMa PET imaging is able to detect LN metastases in areas that have not been covered by a "blind" lymph drainage field and therefore may lead to a better local control of the disease.
68Ga PSNA PET imaging can help to individualize the treatment of prostate cancer patients after RPE and LNE.
